title: duration-aware cartography runner and telemetry normalizer with tail-sample annotator
author: Marisol Chen
description:
Motivation: We need a repeatable runner that maps workload duration distributions (not just sequence lengths) to realistic scheduling and kernel-selection telemetry so the profiling baselines reflect production tail behaviors. This PR introduces a Duration-Aware Cartography Runner that synthesizes mixed-duration sessions, a Telemetry Normalizer that reconciles sampling jitter vs. true latency percentiles, and a Tail-Sample Annotator that tags sampled traces with causality signals for downstream analysis.

Design summary: The runner builds a histogram-based duration cartography from seeded session traces or synthetic generators, then replays requests with a variable-open-window inter-arrival model to exercise long-lived KV-cache and kernel timeouts. The telemetry normalizer post-processes raw traces, applying jitter deconvolution and a moving-window retention filter to produce stable p50/p95/p99 values across repeat runs. The annotator extracts causal markers (prime/warmup/steady/eviction) and writes an enriched CSV/Parquet artifact for reporting pipelines.

What's included: - New runner binary under bench/cartography/runner.go that accepts --seed-file, --duration-histogram, --open-window-ms, --kv-hold-ms flags. - A telemetry normalizer utility (bench/telemetry/normalizer.py) with a small DSL for window policies. - Tail-sample annotator (bench/annotator/annotator.js) used by the reporting pipeline to tag traces for the heatmap exporter. - Unit and integration tests for the runner harness and normalizer. - README with example invocation and expected artifact schema.

Why different from existing workload runners: Existing runners focus on sequence mix or burstiness; this PR intentionally targets duration diversity (sessions that hold KV cache, long streaming replies, background keepalive) and the downstream normalization needed to make p99 comparisons meaningful across hardware/kernel changes.

Rollout plan: Merge to main behind a feature flag (BENCH_CARTOGRAPHY=1). Initial runs gated to the perf-cluster. Collect three baseline runs and compare to the current synthetic-hotspot baseline with the new metric set.

Backwards compatibility: Runner defaults to a conservative, short-duration profile; existing workflows are unaffected unless the feature flag is enabled.

review_comments: Ari Kaplan: Nice approach. Two asks: (1) please add a deterministic mode for the inter-arrival model so we can reproduce exact sequences in perf lab; (2) include a short script that converts Parquet back to CSV for older tooling.
Marisol Chen: Added --deterministic-seed flag and parity CSV output in annotator.js. Also added a note in the README about exact reproduction steps.
Devon Singh: Telemetry normalizer looks promising. Suggest tightening the default moving window to 30s for perf-cluster to avoid state bleed when other jobs run concurrently.
Marisol Chen: Lowered the default window to 30s and added a BENCH_NORMALIZER_WINDOW env override. Also added unit test for the window edge-case.
Priya Nair: LGTM aside from a small lint nit in annotator.js (trailing comma). Will approve after CI passes.
Automated CI: perf-pipeline.yml job initially failed due to missing parquet dependency. Rerun after adding pyarrow pin passes.
merge_result: Merged with squash. Commit message summarized runner, normalizer, and annotator. Baseline artifacts stored under s3://redwood-perf/artifacts/cartography/2025-11-10/.
release_notes: Introduce Duration-Aware Cartography Runner and Telemetry Normalizer: adds duration-focused workload generation and normalized telemetry artifacts to improve p99 stability testing. Opt-in via BENCH_CARTOGRAPHY feature flag.
